PC:
Prepares an appropriate operation room set-up for performing deep sedation:
Places nasal cannula with end-tidal CO2 monitoring capability
Has appropriate size bag and mask, handle and blade, LMA, and endotracheal tube available
Places standard ASA monitors appropriately

Administers deep sedation with assistance:
Chooses the sedative and both the appropriate dose and route for administration

Initiates management under supervision:
Performs anesthesia induction or deep sedation with assistance
Administers appropriate anesthetic or sedative agents and appropriate doses
Attempts airway control
Controls the airway while maintaining general anesthesia (with LMA or endotracheal tube) or deep sedation (jaw thrust and chin lift) for retrobulbar hemorrhage repair
Learner should assess patient, including brief assessment of airway, cardiovascular, pulmonary, and neurologic systems.
Learner should provide oxygen to the patient via mask or nasal cannula, ideally with end tidal CO2 monitoring in place.
Learner should administer sedation or other comfort measures.
Learner should continue to monitor the patient during the block.
Learner should inform the patient of the situation and induce either general anesthesia or deep sedation for emergent retrobulbar hemorrhage repair.
Learner should develop an induction plan and begin to induce general anesthesia or deep sedation.
Learner should pre-oxygenate the patient with a face mask
Learner should induce general anesthesia with any of the available IV anesthetics
Learner should intubate the patient with endotracheal intubation or an LMA.
Learner should provide deep sedation with monitored anesthesia care.
MK:
Identifies patient specific complications with supervision:
Verbalizes a plan for general anesthesia or deep sedation for repair of retrobulbar hemorrhage with assistance
Verbalizes the need for deep but short lasting sedation for the procedure
Verbalizes retrobulbar hemorrhage as complications of retrobulbar block
Verbalizes the potential need for repair of retrobulbar hemorrhage
Verbalizes the different anesthetic options to facilitate the repair of retrobulbar hemorrhage
Learner should identify potential retrobulbar hemorrhage as a cause for proptosis and pain.
ICS: Introduces self to the surgical team at the beginning of procedure
Clearly asks the surgeon about the magnitude of the retrobulbar hemorrhage
Discusses patient’s condition and treatment options with the surgeon in a clear manner
Plays a team leader role in management
Gives clear instructions to other team members in a non-threatening calm manner if assistance is needed (e.g. squeeze the bag once every 6 seconds while I am providing a two hand-mask)
Gives positive feedback to other team members (e.g. good job squeezing that bag)
Learner should inform the surgeons when the patient is appropriately sedated to perform the block.
Learner should discuss the situation with the surgeon.
